headline: Law transfers about 7 acres of Vicksburg National Military Park land to Mississippi, free of charge, for an interpretive center.
what_it_does: The Department of the Interior must give about 7 acres of land, in two parcels, inside Vicksburg National Military Park to the state of Mississippi for an interpretive center. The land is given at no cost through a quitclaim deed. The land must help the public get into the park, cannot be used in ways that harm the park's resources or visitors' experience, and stays subject to any use limits Interior sets. After the transfer, the park's official boundary will be redrawn to leave out this land.

who_it_affects.how: The state receives about 7 acres of former park land at no cost to build an interpretive center, subject to use limits.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to Vicksburg National Military Park
who_it_affects.how: The transferred land must be used to make it easier for the public to get into the park and may not harm the visitor experience.

who_it_affects.group: National Park Service (Department of the Interior)
who_it_affects.how: The agency must transfer the land, set any use restrictions, and change the park's boundary to exclude it.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 20, 2026; the boundary change happens once the land is transferred, and no specific deadline is stated in the summary.
